title: Etienne Bourdeaux to Maarten van der Goes, Berlin, 31 January 1801 (DECODE R1944)

documents.shelfmark: Nationaal Archief, 2.01.08, Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken 1796-1810, inv. 257, fol. 294; DECODE R1944

plaintext.source: Ministry clear copy of no. 16, fol. 295, imaged as DECODE R1946 image 3 (IMG_R1946_I13417_P3.png).

transcription.source: Authenticated DECODE scans of R1944 and R1946.
transcription.notes: Only the clear copy was transcribed; group count (about 110) estimated by eye from the two cipher images, not measured. Corrections: 'vertrek' -> 'renvoy', 'positiver' -> 'positiever' on second reading.

system.summary: A numerical Dutch diplomatic nomenclator of one- to three-digit groups with superposed marks, attributed by DECODE to S. E. Croiset.

diacritics.note: Bars, ticks, waves, dots and crosses over the figures.

system.notes: Key not identified; groups not aligned to the clear copy.

prior_solution.where: The ministry's clear copy, fol. 295, misfiled under DECODE R1946.

conditions.human_role: Supplied authenticated DECODE access and posed the target.

solution.what: Retrieved the two R1944 scans: cipher groups only, with closing and signature.
Viewed the neighbouring records R1945 and R1946; R1946 image 3 is a clear sheet headed N. 16, Berlyn 31 January 1801, (get.) Bourdeaux.
Re-read the scan (corrected renvoy, positiever); checked consecutive folio stamps 294/295 and that ~90 words fit ~110 code groups.

outcome.method_basis: The ministry's contemporary clear copy of the despatch (fol. 295, N. 16, Berlin 31 Jan 1801) was found misfiled as image 3 of DECODE R1946 and transcribed; the code groups were not decoded.
outcome.notes: Plaintext from the contemporary clear copy; the code was not decoded group by group.
